thread:
Priya: Walked past the whiteboard and someone drew a compiler error as a sandwich. Why are we like this. :sandwich:
Ben: Because sandwiches have layers and so do error messages. Also it was mine, guilty. :joy:
Zoe: In my defense the sandwich had an `unexpected token` pickle. Very crunchy.
Chris: Can we start naming microservices after sandwiches? `panini-auth` sounds secure.
Priya: Only if the deployment pipeline requires you to eat the sandwich before merging. Food-based CI. :fork_and_knife:
Ben: Found a config snippet in the kitchen that would make any parser cry:```yaml
condiments:
	mustard: true
  ketchup: false
```
Zoe: Tabs + spaces in YAML = the forbidden fusion cuisine.
LintBot: @channel lint warning: `tabs detected in YAML` — recommended action: convert to spaces or accept spicy failures. :warning:
Chris: LintBot, previous PRs show you flagged `semver: relaxed` once. Is that allowed?
LintBot: @Chris semantic versioning mode set to `lenient` for dev branch. Consequence: versions like `0.1-sandwich` accepted. Proceed with caution.
Priya: We should adopt a naming convention: feature branches are sandwiches, hotfixes are snacks.
Ben: Proposal: semver for sandwiches: major = ingredients changed, minor = new sauce, patch = toasted. Example: `2.0.1-toasted-basil`.
Zoe: I will accept `toasted-basil` as a valid pre-release tag. Also there should be an RFC about intolerances.
Chris: If the compiler emits `segmentation fault` do we call housekeeping or medical? :thinking_face:
Priya: Housekeeping. They handle crumbs.
Ben: Also whoever wrote `ketchup: false` is on dish duty. That's non-negotiable. :grin:
Zoe: TL;DR: lunch will now be used to settle merge conflicts. Bring bread.
LintBot: Fun fact: most YAML-related incidents happen between 11:30 and 13:30 local time. Please hydrate and indent responsibly. :droplet:
